1.explanation: The Kotlin language definition file (kotlin.js) in src/languages contains the grammar rules for tokenizing Kotlin source code. In its current state, the rules around class headers and the colon-based inheritance syntax are causing the braces to be assigned an incorrect or inconsistent token class. Fixing or extending the grammar in kotlin.js to properly recognize and treat those braces identically to other block braces will resolve the inconsistent highlighting.
1.bug_scenario: When using highlight.js to render Kotlin code with class inheritance (e.g. "class TABLE: Tag { ... }"), the opening and closing curly braces around the class body are tokenized differently in this context and thus highlighted with a different color than other braces. In the provided screenshot, the braces immediately following the colon and type parameter are highlighted in a distinct color compared with the braces of other classes.

2.explanation: The Kotlin language definition (`src/languages/kotlin.js`) contains the mode patterns that recognize class declarations, bodies and punctuation (braces). Any mis-scoping or incorrect mode placement there will cause braces to be tokenized differently. Additionally, the `multi_class` extension (`src/lib/ext/multi_class.js`) is used across languages to parse class inheritance and may include regex or mode logic that scopes braces around inherited classes incorrectly. Fixing or adjusting the class pattern in `kotlin.js` or the inheritance handling in `multi_class.js` will ensure those braces are tokenized as regular punctuation and highlighted uniformly.
